main_text.head: AD CAROLVM COSSÆVM BRIXIACI DYNASTAM, post captas Vercellas.
main_text.p: VIS me niuosos &[?] Alpium trâs vertices Curru volucri deferet? Quis nube septum me remotis Pegasus Sistet iugis Oenotriæ? Non ut parentum laude Romam, vel sua Virtute Venetum nobilem Fratrisve flammis, & fororum lachrymis Padum calentem conspicer. Sed te beatæ, lux beata, Gallia Cossæe[?], propius ut colam, Te mirer Italum, te Pelasgum gloriam, Splendore fuscantem nouo, Ceu Sol Dianam, ceu Diana cæteras Obscurat astrorum faces. Nec pectus hac mi perculit cupidine Florentis ævi gloria, Seu pertinacem cum Batauum impelleres Sæua tremendus cuspide, Qualis columbas spergit imbelles fuga Ales minister fulminis.

page.notes: The large initial V of "VIS" is a woodcut ornament, joined to the word. "Coffæe" reads as Cossæe (long s printed like f), marked [?]. The symbol before "Alpium" is unclear and marked [?]. The "F. ij." mark is a gathering signature. The verse is one continuous block with no stanza breaks, so it is one paragraph with the printed line breaks removed.
